candidates.label: Drug-induced organizing pneumonia (secondary to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole)
missing_or_uncertain: Confirmation of drug causality (e.g., eosinophilia, drug rechallenge)

candidates.label: Post-infectious organizing pneumonia (following Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia)
missing_or_uncertain: Temporal relationship to infection, exclusion of other causes

candidates.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonitis
missing_or_uncertain: CMV PCR or antigenemia, biopsy with viral inclusions

candidates.label: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis
missing_or_uncertain: Galactomannan, fungal culture, biopsy with hyphae

candidates.label: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD)
missing_or_uncertain: EBV PCR, biopsy with monoclonal proliferation

response.rationale: The patient developed new pulmonary infiltrates three weeks into TMP-SMX therapy, after initial resolution of PCP. Repeat BAL was negative for AFB, fungus, and PJP, and biopsy showed alveoli filled with inflammatory debris, most consistent with organizing pneumonia. The temporal association with TMP-SMX suggests drug-induced etiology, though post-infectious organizing pneumonia is also plausible. Other infections and PTLD are less likely given negative BAL and biopsy findings.
